recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up core source work is needed for FHIR-39096 unless the work group later decides to reopen message identity semantics; do not duplicate the existing FHIR-40518/FHIR-40519 audit commits.
issue_request: FHIR-39096 asked the R5 messaging page to stop using Bundle.id and MessageHeader.id for logical message identity, state that an incoming message has exactly one Bundle.identifier, update reliable messaging resend/cache rules to use Bundle.identifier, add MessageHeader usage guidance, and clarify the REST relationship.
initial_application: The issue was applied by git 87b1af3c09 after preparatory commit 5e04fe1f02, changing source/messaging.html and source/messageheader/messageheader-notes.xml. Prior commit bce22083f1 from FHIR-29690 had already aligned MessageHeader.response.identifier with Bundle.identifier.
additional_context: The February 2023 Zulip thread and Confluence minutes show the work-group discussion and vote supporting Bundle.identifier as the single message identity. Later commits b667d192f3 and 749bbcaef2 refined the REST wording and added an implementer note without reversing the decision. Related FHIR-40518 and FHIR-40519 were implemented in the same historical commit and are already audited on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. Current messaging.html contains the required Bundle.identifier identity text, retry/cache table, response-correlation wording, REST relationship paragraph, and implementer note; current MessageHeader notes contain the required no-persistent-identifier sentence.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Published issue changed MessageHeader.response.identifier to refer to Bundle.identifier, providing prerequisite context for FHIR-39096.
Older id/identifier confusion tracker was resolved as Not Persuasive because it was dealt with as part of FHIR-39096.
Zero-or-more response wording was voted and applied in the same historical messaging commit and already has a combined-branch audit commit.
Transfer-protocol wording was voted and applied in the same historical messaging commit and already has a combined-branch audit commit.
